extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.publisher: IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Independent, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University
extraction.citeAs: Yue, X., Ni, Y., Zhang, K., Zheng, T., Liu, R., Zhang, G., Stevens, S., Jiang, D., Ren, W., Sun, Y., Wei, C., Yu, B., Yuan, R., Sun, R., Yin, M., Zheng, B., Yang, Z., Liu, Y., Huang, W., Sun, H., Su, Y., & Chen, W. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection takes three stages. Firstly, selecting subjects based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted. Secondly, recruiting over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in these majors as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators adhered to copyright and license regulations and selected questions without immediately available answers to avoid data contamination. This resulted in a diverse collection of 13K questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format. Problems were categorized into four difficulty levels, and approximately 10% classified as 'very easy' were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format, with corrections undertaken where deviations were found.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected questions following guidelines detailed in Appendix A/H. Guidelines included: all questions must contain images, be in English, meet college-level difficulty, be unambiguous, and categorize question type/difficulty/image type. Data format was JSON. Ambiguities were flagged for team review. Ethical considerations included avoiding copyright issues and private information. Data contamination was addressed by selecting questions with non-obvious answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for a detailed review process and collaboratively examined in team meetings to establish a standardized approach for annotation. A secondary review team rigorously vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 primary annotation per item, followed by rigorous vetting by a secondary review team.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in the selected majors.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity tools (for deduplication).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioning information is provided in a Version Change Log (Appendix J), detailing changes from V1 to V4. A live-updating leaderboard is maintained.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Expert AGI could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. The benchmark helps monitor progress towards Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. There lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults'. College exams are not the only tasks an AGI shall tackle.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation and testing of multimodal models on college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.
